chunks: Muhammad ibn al-'Is asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
Do I have intercourse while I am naked? He said: 'Yes, and also facing the Qibla and also turning one's back to it.'
And Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not have intercourse in the ship.'

And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is disliked for a man to cover/lie with his wife when he has had a nocturnal emission until he performs ghusl from the emission he saw. If he does so and the child is born insane, let him not blame anyone but himself.'

key_terms.غَشَى: To cover / To lie with (in marital context)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended etiquettes and disliked actions regarding marital intercourse in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, drawn from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, details specific etiquette (adab) for marital intimacy, prohibiting intercourse while naked or facing/turning away from the Qibla, and advising against it on ships. It further links the state of major ritual impurity (janabah) from nocturnal emission to the potential for offspring to be born insane if intercourse occurs before the required ghusl, emphasizing the spiritual and physical consequences of neglecting ritual purity.
